official.description: The Konstanty Kalinowski Scholarship Programme is a Polish Government scholarship programme addressed in particular to socially and politically active citizens of Belarus who cannot continue their education in their own country because of their political activity. It offers scholarships for bachelor's, master's and doctoral studies as well as research internships and postgraduate studies in all fields of study, and runs two strands: Programme KK I for studies at institutions across Poland and Programme KK II for one-year research stays in Warsaw.
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme for Belarusian students unable to continue their education in Belarus

verification.notes: The URL stored in the catalogue (study.gov.pl/konstanty-kalinowski-scholarship-programme) returns HTTP 404. The live official pages are the Government of Poland portal and the NAWA-operated study.gov.pl scholarship overview, both of which were read directly. Neither publishes a monetary figure. The programme operator's site, studium.uw.edu.pl, was unreachable across four attempts, so the current call folder could not be checked. Note that the catalogue description listing Georgia, Ukraine, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Moldova does not match the official description: the official pages address the programme specifically to citizens of Belarus.

applicant_utility.summary: This programme is not a general Eastern Partnership scholarship - the official pages address it specifically to citizens of Belarus who cannot continue their education because of their political activity, so check that framing before you invest time in an application. There is no published stipend figure on the Government or NAWA pages, and the actual formal requirements and document list live in the Programme folders on the Studium Europy Wschodniej UW site, so treat that folder as the real application brief. Recruitment has run continuously since 31 August 2020 until the place limit is exhausted, which means you apply when you are ready rather than waiting for a window - but it also means places can run out without notice.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Belarusian citizens who have been expelled from or blocked from Belarusian higher education for political reasons and want to begin or continue a degree or research stay in Poland.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you fit the programme's stated target group - socially and politically active Belarusian citizens unable to continue their education in Belarus - because that framing is the eligibility gate
Locate and read the current Programme folder on studium.uw.edu.pl; it is the only place the formal requirements and required documents are published
Decide early whether you are applying for Programme KK I (degree studies across Poland) or Programme KK II (a one-year research stay in Warsaw), because they are separate recruitments
Email bialorus.studium@uw.edu.pl before submitting to confirm places are still available, since recruitment is capped by a place limit rather than a deadline
Prepare your academic record and evidence of your Belarusian study situation in advance, as these will be central to the application
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the programme is open to all Eastern Partnership nationals; the official pages address it specifically to Belarusian applicants
Relying on aggregator pages that quote a monthly stipend - no figure is published on the awarding body's own pages
Submitting without reading the Programme folder on studium.uw.edu.pl, which is where the formal requirements and document list actually live
Applying too late in a continuous recruitment that is capped by a place limit rather than a deadline
Confusing Programme KK I and Programme KK II and preparing for the wrong strand
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published. The Government and NAWA pages reached do not state what the scholarship covers or excludes, so you cannot budget from them - confirm the coverage explicitly with the Programme Director before accepting a place.
document_audit: No document list is published on the Government of Poland portal or on study.gov.pl - the requirements sit in the Programme folders on studium.uw.edu.pl

The Government portal points to studium.uw.edu.pl for all formal requirements; if that site is unreachable, email bialorus.studium@uw.edu.pl for the folder rather than relying on second-hand summaries
Be ready to evidence your inability to continue education in Belarus, since that is the programme's stated basis
